source.text: BUSI 628. | 1.5 Credits. | Prerequisite, BUSI 510 , HPM 300 ; Pre- or corequisite, BUSI 411 .

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Applied Learning: Symposium Core Committee
courses.description: Permission of the department. This course is by invitation only to students who previously served on the Undergraduate Business Symposium core committee. As senior advisors, students practice the leadership, organization, delegation, communication, and teamwork skills that they learn about in their other courses.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Applied Trading Strategies
courses.description: This seminar style course develops a set of financial tools useful for trading primary and derivative securities with the goal of obtaining specific exposures in equity, fixed income, and commodity markets. The course examines methods for managing financial price risk of positions and how hedge funds use derivatives in practice. Honors version available.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Honors Research Proposal
courses.description: Permission of the department. Open to senior business administration majors with a minimum 3.5 grade point average in business courses. Students learn business research techniques and develop individual proposals for business research. Successful proposals may advance to honors thesis research and writing ( BUSI 692H ).

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Honors Thesis
courses.description: Permission of the department. Open to senior business majors with a minimum 3.5 grade point average in business courses. Original investigation of a topic in business and preparation of a substantive research project under the direction of a faculty advisor. Written essay and oral presentation are required.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Artistic Entrepreneurship
courses.description: This course is a study in entrepreneurship and the specific challenges faced by artistic entrepreneurs.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Introduction to Social Entrepreneurship
courses.description: An overview of how entrepreneurship is transforming students' fields and disciplines and how the application of principles of entrepreneurship may be used to advance their professional objectives.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Introduction to Commercial Entrepreneurship
courses.description: A cross-disciplinary curriculum that brings together the core field with the wide-ranging literature in entrepreneurship to seek new approaches to traditional problems.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Entrepreneurship Capstone
courses.description: Capstone project, business plan, or paper that links the work done in the certificate to the field it is intended to complement.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Entrepreneurship Capstone Project
courses.description: This Graduate Certificate in Entrepreneurship capstone project is self-paced, and overseen by the faculty director of each track (life sciences, public health, and artistic).

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study intends to extend a student's learning beyond the classroom or allows a student the opportunity to explore a topic not offered in a traditional format.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Applied Research Methods I
courses.description: Addresses fundamentals of empirical social science research. Topics include framing a research question, comparing research designs, instrumentation, reliability, validity, and exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis. Emphasizes application and analysis.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Applied Research Methods II
courses.description: Continuation of BUSI 808 . Topics include statistical control, categorical variables, interaction, curvilinear and similarity effects, longitudinal analysis, path analysis, structural equation modeling, and publication. Emphasizes application and analysis.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Empirical Operations
courses.description: Required preparation, working knowledge of probability, statistics, and regression. The course prepares students to perform academic research, and it will be conducted in a manner that simulates an academic research conference. The course will focus on empirical research approaches used in solving many classical problems in operations management.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Theory of Operations Management I
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Rigorous study of traditional and modern issues, problems, and approaches in operations management.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Theory of Operations Management II
courses.description: A continuation of BUSI 830 .

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Theory of Operations Management III
courses.description: A continuation of BUSI 830 .

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Operations Management
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Intensive study of a specific area in operations management.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Seminar in Operations Management
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Intensive study of a specific area in operations management.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Individual Behavior in Organizations
courses.description: Analysis of individual behavior, adjustment, and effectiveness. Examination of attitudes, stress, problem solving, decision making, motivation, and personality. Applications to management of human resources.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Interpersonal and Intergroup Behavior in Business Organizations
courses.description: Intensive critical examination of interpersonal and intergroup behavior, including decision processes, communication, conflict, and conflict resolution in large organizations.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Macro Organizational Behavior
courses.description: Graduate standing in business administration required. Intensive study of theory and research in organizational structure, coordinating and control mechanisms, design parameters, and environments.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Organizational Design and Development
courses.description: The development of understanding and skills in changing and evolving organizational design, interpersonal relationships, and people to achieve organizational goals.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Seminar in Organizational Behavior
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Intensive study of important current theory and research in organizational behavior.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Seminar in Human Resource Management
courses.description: Review the research literature on how firms are made more effective through their people. Coverage includes topics like recruitment, hiring, compensation, socialization, culture, and performance management.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Special Topics in Organizational Behavior
courses.description: BUSI 858 is a second doctoral course in organizational behavior, meant to be taken after completing BUSI 851 : Individual Behavior in Organizations. While BUSI 851 gave an overview of many important topics in organizational behavior, the field is too broad to be covered, in depth, with a single class. The goal of this course is to introduce developing scholars to the history and current status of important topics in organizational behavior. This course is intended for developing scholars who intend to pursue academic careers.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Seminar in Marketing I
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Overview of current paradigms and research in marketing. Topics include philosophy of science, differing views of what marketing is, strengths and weaknesses of various research approaches, and career socialization issues.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Seminar in Marketing II
courses.description: Intensive study of the empirical and analytical literature involving problems in pricing, product development and management, advertising and promotion, distribution, and strategy.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Marketing Models
courses.description: This class covers a range of econometric principles and models of relevance to marketing. The emphasis will be on model formulation and estimation.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Seminar in Current Marketing Topics
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Advanced research in marketing. A seminar to discuss current research of doctoral candidates, faculty, and invited guests.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Issues in the Design and Analysis of Research in Marketing
courses.description: Graduate standing in business administration required. A review of major issues in marketing, including philosophy of science, measurement, and experimental and quasi-experimental design.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Seminar in Marketing Research Methodology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. An introduction to multivariate data analysis methods including factor analysis, cluster analysis, logic, discriminant analysis and multidimensional scaling.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Seminar in Research in Accounting
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. An informal seminar to discuss current research in accounting.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Financial Economics
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Introduction to the theories of asset pricing.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Corporate Finance
courses.description: Introduction to corporate finance theory.

courses.title: Empirical Corporate Finance

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Seminar in Research in Finance
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Advanced research in business finance and investment. An informal seminar to discuss current research of doctoral candidates, faculty, and others.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Introduction to Empirical Finance
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the quantitative methods used in empirical asset pricing. Model specification and estimation issues are discussed at length. The course emphasizes both theoretical and practical research.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Quantitative Methods in Finance
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Review of information generating and optimizing models and their applicability to decision making in finance.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Seminar in Financial Markets
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Advanced methods in finance.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Strategic Management Overview
courses.description: A seminar to provide a broad and current understanding of strategic management. Exposure to the entire field is emphasized.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Strategic Formulation
courses.description: This seminar emphasizes both process and content issues to provide students with an in-depth understanding of strategy formulation topics.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.title: Strategy Implementation
courses.description: This seminar focuses on strategy implementation, with particular emphasis devoted to the process, systems, and structures required for effective implementation.
